title: Operator automation rollout (Q3 2025) — postmortem and action plan
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:

In Q3 2025 we rolled out the first global version of the Operator Automation feature (v1.0) across production regions. Operator Automation is a set of automated remediation workflows that detect degraded inference worker pools and apply corrective actions (scale, restart, route around) without requiring manual intervention. The rollout aimed to reduce mean time to repair (MTTR) for common transient faults and to lower cognitive load on on-call operators.

Unfortunately, within 48 hours of enabling the feature by default for all tenants, we observed repeated SLO burn for background and interactive text-generation requests in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Multiple customers reported elevated 95th percentile latency and several internal SLIs crossed the 1% error budget threshold.

This document summarizes the timeline, root causes, key contributing factors, mitigations applied during the incident, and a prioritized action plan with owners and deadlines. It also captures recommendations for safer automation rollouts and a proposed validation suite for future releases.

Impact:

- Regions affected: us-west-2 (primary), eu-west-1 (secondary).
- Customer impact: ~7 customers experienced >10% increase in 95p latency for generation endpoints; 2 customers had temporary degraded SLAs (billing credits applied).
- SLO metrics: 95p response latency SLO (<= 200ms) breached by 18% for a 3-hour window on 2025-10-07. Error budget consumption spiked 12% across the platform during the incident week.
- MTTR: Initial mitigation took ~210 minutes to stabilize traffic after rollback.

Timeline (chronological):

1) 2025-10-05 02:00 UTC — Canary rollout of Operator Automation v1.0 to 10% of non-prod and a single canary tenant in us-west-2. Observability signals stable.
2) 2025-10-06 18:30 UTC — Gradual promotion to 100% of non-prod and 50% of production tenant traffic via feature flag. No immediate anomalies.
3) 2025-10-07 03:10 UTC — Automated remediation triggers: operator-autoremediation started automated rebalancing of KV cache shards on several GPU nodes. Remediation entailed ephemeral process restarts and temporary eviction of in-memory prefixes.
4) 2025-10-07 03:40 UTC — Platform dashboards show correlated 95p latency increase (us-west-2). Several rate-limited retries from client SDKs amplified traffic spikes.
5) 2025-10-07 05:00 UTC — On-call notified via pager for slo-burn alert (operator.slo_burn > 5% over 30m).
6) 2025-10-07 06:40 UTC — Emergency rollback of Operator Automation feature flag in us-west-2 and eu-west-1; traffic stabilized by 06:50 UTC.
7) 2025-10-07 07:30 UTC — Post-rollback validation and targeted remediation complete.

Root causes and contributing factors:

Primary root causes (direct):
- Aggressive automation sequence that performed concurrent KV shard eviction and instance-level restarts without global rate limiting. This caused synchronized regeneration of KV caches across many replicas, producing a temporary surge in CPU/GPU memory pressure and I/O which increased tail latency.
- Automation algorithm assumed a soft window of 30s between dependent actions; in production observed interleaving that created a thundering-herd effect.

Secondary contributors (systemic & process):
- Canary surface and traffic shaping did not model multi-tenant retry amplification; canary tenants had lower retry rates and different client SDK versions compared to many real customers.
- Dashboards lacked a causal decomposition view combining KV-cache-regeneration events with tenant-level retry patterns. Operators could see SLOs and node CPU but not the causal link quickly enough.
- No global automation circuit breaker that would stop concurrent remediations above an operational concurrency threshold per-region.
- Runbook and escalation playbooks assumed manual operator intervention for restarts, so automation had less conservative safety checks.

Immediate mitigations taken during the incident:

- Feature flag rollback to disable Operator Automation across affected regions (2025-10-07 06:40 UTC).
- Throttling introduced at the request ingress layer for traffic from SDKs with high retry rates to dampen amplification while rollback completed.
- Short-term dashboard added: operator.autoremediation.activity showing "in-flight" remediation count and per-tenant KV-eviction events.

Detailed timeline of mitigations and diagnostic commands used by operators (runbook excerpts):

1) Verify automation state and in-flight remediation (internal API):

curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $PLATFORM_OP_TOKEN" https://platform-api.internal/operator-autoremediation/status | jq

2) List nodes under eviction pressure and tail-latency contributors:

kubectl -n runtime get pods -l app=worker -o wide
kubectl -n runtime top pods --containers | grep worker

3) To temporarily mark a region as automation-disabled from operator console CLI:

redwood ops automation disable --region us-west-2 --reason "post-rollback stabilization"

Runbook for emergency rollback (condensed):

1) Pin feature flag to OFF via LaunchDarkly (or internal flag service).
2) Confirm disabled state across all regions: query operator-autoremediation/status for all regions.
3) Re-route priority tenants to dedicated pool if degradation persists: redwood routing promote --tenant $TENANT_ID --pool dedicated-pool-1
4) Monitor slo-dashboard/95p-latency and autoremediation.activity until values return to baseline for 30m.

Lessons learned and recommended changes (short, medium, long term):

Short term (<= 30 days):
- Implement a per-region automation concurrency limiter and soft circuit-breaker that prevents >N concurrent remediations (default N=3). Owner: Ramon Alvarez. Due: 2025-11-01.
- Expand canary traffic profiles to include synthetic retry amplification tests that emulate worst-case SDK behaviour. Owner: QA/Platform SRE. Due: 2025-11-05.
- Add an observability dashboard that shows correlation between automation events and tenant-level retry rates (operator.autoremediation.causal-map). Owner: Observability team. Due: 2025-10-20.

Medium term (30–90 days):
- Introduce staged remediation orchestration with exponential backoff between dependent actions and randomized jitter windows. Owner: Serving Runtime. Due: 2026-01-10.
- Implement an automation safety harness with offline simulation capability (runbook-sim) that replays historical traffic and measures expected tail-latency impact. Owner: Applied ML & Evals. Due: 2026-01-31.

Long term (>90 days):
- Policy: All automation rollouts that can affect KV caches or memory must pass a stability gate that includes: synthetic amplification tests, replay simulation, and a chaos-probing run in staging. Owner: Eng Platform. Due: 2026-04-01.
- Product change: Expose an "automation-sensitivity" tenant preference so customers can opt into conservative automation behavior for regulated workloads. Owner: Product. Due: 2026-06-01.

Prioritized action items (table):

| Priority | Action | Owner | Due | Status |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| P0 | Implement per-region automation concurrency limiter and circuit-breaker | Ramon Alvarez | 2025-11-01 | in_progress |
| P0 | Create synthetic retry-amplification canary profile and add to CI pipeline | QA/Platform SRE | 2025-11-05 | todo |
| P1 | Add "autoremediation.causal-map" dashboard and alert | Observability Team | 2025-10-20 | done |
| P1 | Add exponential backoff + jitter to remediation sequences | Serving Runtime | 2026-01-10 | todo |
| P2 | Build offline runbook-sim and validation harness | Applied ML & Evals | 2026-01-31 | todo |

Metrics and dashboards to track going forward:

- operator.autoremediation.inflight_count (gauge) — target: <= 3 per-region by default.
- operator.autoremediation.throttle_rate (counter) — shows how often circuit-breaker engages.
- slo.95p.latency.by-region (timeseries) — monitor for deviation from baseline.
- tenant.retry.amplification.index — synthetic metric introduced to quantify a tenant's retry behavior.

Example alert rule (Prometheus-style pseudo):

alert: OperatorAutomationConcurrentRemediations
expr: operator_autoremediation_inflight_count{region="us-west-2"} > 3
for: 5m
labels: {severity="major", team="eng-platform"}
annotations: {summary=">3 concurrent remediations in us-west-2"}

Communication and customer handling:

- Immediately after rollback we notified impacted customers via standard incident template and offered a follow-up technical review. Two customers requested dedicated debrief sessions which were completed by 2025-11-20.
- Applied goodwill credits where SLAs were breached. Finance and Customer Success coordinated credits and post-incident outreach.

Appendix — quick diagnostic checklist for oncall operators (cheat-sheet):

1) Check automation status: curl https://platform-api.internal/operator-autoremediation/status
2) If inflight_count > 3 in the region, consider disabling automation and promote priority tenants to dedicated pools.
3) To re-enable automation for a region after stabilization: redwood ops automation enable --region <region> --dry-run; monitor operator.autoremediation.inflight_count for 60 minutes.
4) Escalation: if SLOs remain degraded > 60 minutes after rollback, page Eng Platform lead and SRE manager (pager codes listed in Oncall directory).
